source: Morais O., Cargill C., Parke K. and Barnes T. 2020. Smallholder Pig Production Technicians' Manual. Timor-Leste Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries, University of Queensland, ACIAR and the TOMAK Program (Australian Aid), Dili.
text: Select gilts (future sows) from litters born to the herd's best sows — those that farrow the most piglets per litter and whose piglets are the fastest-growing and heaviest at weaning (5–8 weeks). Choose several of the fastest-growing females from the best litters at weaning, feed them a balanced diet while growing, and make the final selection around 6 months of age. Good traits to look for: a long body from head to tail with well-rounded hams, sound legs (even toes, not walking on toes, correct leg angle), and at least 10 good teats (12 is better). Selling the strongest, healthiest females from the best sows for meat instead of keeping them for breeding, or breeding from smaller/weaker piglets, will make the herd worse over time.
caveat: This guidance comes from a Timor-Leste smallholder pig manual, not a Cambodia-specific source. Feed ingredients and general husbandry practices transfer well to Cambodia's tropical smallholder conditions, but local breed weights/ages and disease-context details may differ; confirm specifics with a local vet or extension officer where precision matters.
